title: Catch-up and revision: lessons 1 to 10
footer: 1.2 Lesson 11: Catch-up and revision: lessons 1 to 10
starter: Without notes, write down the eight units of storage in order, and the eight place values of an 8-bit number.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Primary storage
facts: RAM: volatile, read/write, holds what's in use.
ROM: non-volatile, read-only, holds the boot program.
Primary storage is directly accessible by the CPU.
stations.challenge: State two differences between RAM and ROM.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: RAM: volatile, read/write, holds what's in use.
Also credit: ROM: non-volatile, read-only, holds the boot program.

questions.q: Which is volatile?
What does ROM hold?
What does primary storage mean?
questions.a: Memory the CPU can access directly

stations.name: Virtual memory
facts: Secondary storage used as extra RAM when RAM is full.
Data is swapped in and out as the CPU needs it.
Much slower than RAM, so more RAM is the real fix.
stations.challenge: Explain why virtual memory slows a computer down.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Secondary storage used as extra RAM when RAM is full.
Also credit: Data is swapped in and out as the CPU needs it.

questions.q: When is virtual memory used?
Why is virtual memory slow?
questions.a: Secondary storage is much slower than RAM

questions.q: What is the best way to reduce the use of virtual memory?

stations.name: Secondary storage
facts: Magnetic: platters and a read/write head; cheap and huge.
Optical: a laser reading pits and lands; cheap and portable.
Solid state: flash memory; fast and durable but dearer.
stations.challenge: Name a suitable device for a laptop and justify it.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Magnetic: platters and a read/write head; cheap and huge.
Also credit: Optical: a laser reading pits and lands; cheap and portable.

questions.q: Which type has no moving parts?
Which is cheapest per gigabyte for very large amounts of data?
Which would you choose for a video camera's storage?

stations.name: Units and capacity
facts: Bit, nibble (4), byte (8), then kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, each ×1,000.
Image size = width × height × colour depth.
Sound size = sample rate × bit depth × duration.
stations.challenge: Calculate the size of a 400 × 300 image at 8 bits per pixel.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Bit, nibble (4), byte (8), then kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, each ×1,000.
Also credit: Image size = width × height × colour depth.

questions.q: How many bytes are in 3 kB?
What is the formula for image file size?
A sound is 8,000 Hz, 8-bit, 10 seconds. What is its size in bits?

stations.name: Binary and addition
facts: MSB is leftmost, LSB is rightmost.
8 bits hold 0 to 255; anything larger overflows.
stations.challenge: Convert 173 to binary and add 00001111 to it.
challengeAnswer: Also credit: MSB is leftmost, LSB is rightmost.

questions.q: What is 10011100 in denary?
What is the largest number 8 bits can hold?
When does an overflow error occur?
questions.a: When the result needs more bits than are available

stations.name: Shifts and hex
facts: Left shift ×2 per place; right shift ÷2 per place.
One hex digit is exactly 4 bits.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Left shift ×2 per place; right shift ÷2 per place.
Also credit: One hex digit is exactly 4 bits.

questions.q: A left shift of 1 place does what?
What is 1111 in hexadecimal?
How many bits does one hex digit represent?

final.name: Final challenge: mixed practice

questions.q: Convert 149 into 8-bit binary.
Add these two binary numbers, ticking overflow if needed.
questions.a: 10110100 + 01011111 = 00010011 (180 + 95 = 275), and the answer needs a 9th bit, so an overflow error occurs

questions.q: Convert 10110010 into hexadecimal.

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

points: RAM: volatile, read/write, holds what's in use.
ROM: non-volatile, read-only, holds the boot program.
Primary storage is directly accessible by the CPU.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark for a correct answer.

exam.q: Explain why a computer uses virtual memory.
points: RAM: volatile, read/write, holds what's in use.
ROM: non-volatile, read-only, holds the boot program.
Primary storage is directly accessible by the CPU.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 3.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
